intro: This guide to Krabi is built from places whose own websites, or the national parks department, publish an address and current details. For the big landscapes, you can start with Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park, headquartered at 79 Moo 5 in Ao Nang, then head inland to Than Bok Khorani in Ao Luek or Khao Phanom Bencha in Thap Prik. The parks department's pages for all three tell you to carry your entrance-fee receipt for inspection and list park welfare shops open daily from 8.30 to 16.30, though those pages carry a 2015 footer.

For islands further south, the parks department's Mu Ko Lanta page, which also carries a 2015 footer, says Ko Rok, Kong Hin Daeng and Kong Hin Muang are closed to tourists from 16 May to 15 November every year, so plan those trips outside that window. Back on the mainland, Ao Nang has the most choice for eating. CRU Kitchen and Bar opens every day from 11:00 to 23:00 and warns that its 68 seats fill up quickly, while Del & Dia Cafe opens daily from 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM for lattes, croissants and breakfast.

For a slower evening, GAIA Kitchen & Bar at Pakasai Resort serves brunch, coffee and cocktails every day from 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with live music on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and MIRA Restaurant at the same resort offers a five-course tasting menu or à la carte. At Nong Thale, Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, lists Lae Lay and Sri Trang for dinner from 6:00 PM to 10:00 PM, Pirom Bar until 11:00 PM, and Jampoon from 6:30 AM, where breakfast is also available for a fee.

Railay works differently. At Railay Village Resort, Krua Village Restaurant serves Thai and Western food but does not sell alcohol, and the resort says you can bring your own without corkage fees. At Rayavadee, The Grotto is the only venue listed as open, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner without alcohol from 07:00 to 21:00, while Krua Phranang, The Raya Dining and Raitalay Terrace are listed as temporarily closed. Sand Sea Resort offers a private candlelit four-course beach dinner for two that you can book.
summaryCards: Start with Hat Noppharat Thara–Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park from Ao Nang, then book dinner at CRU Kitchen and Bar, which opens every day but has only 68 seats.
Del & Dia Cafe in Ao Nang opens daily at 7:00 AM for lattes and croissants, and Jampoon at Phulay Bay serves breakfast from 6:30 AM.
None of the restaurants checked lists a weekly closing day, but Mu Ko Lanta National Park closes Ko Rok, Kong Hin Daeng and Kong Hin Muang to tourists from 16 May to 15 November every year.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and menu details do not guarantee availability. The national parks department pages carry a 2015 footer, so their welfare-shop hours and the Mu Ko Lanta seasonal closure are taken from older pages and no fees are published. Several confirmed resort venues publish only partial details: Dusit Thani Krabi Beach Resort lists hours as "Seasonal", Aonang Villa Resort and Railay Village Resort publish no venue hours, MIRA's page gives conflicting closing times, Lae Lay Grill's page is undated and also says "Always Open", and Nakamanda and Sand Sea restaurant pages are undated. Sites that could not be read: Banyan Tree Krabi, Avani Ao Nang Cliff, Holiday Inn Resort Krabi Ao Nang Beach, Starbucks Thailand and Krabi Town Municipality (403), King Climbers (expired certificate), Sofitel Krabi Phokeethra, Railay Princess, Aonang Cliff Beach Resort and Maharat Bakery (domain errors), Beyond Resort's Krabi bakery (522) and Aonang Villa's Kiang Le page (connection dropped). Rayavadee's other restaurants are listed as temporarily closed, and Centara Grand Krabi appears to be relaunching as Centara Reserve Krabi with stays offered from 1 March 2027. Popular areas such as Railay Beach, Ao Nang beach and the Four Islands trip have no single operator website and are not covered as places.
